subject: Clarify: hold duration for transient session snapshots after incident
body:
From: Tim Browne <tim.browne@acmehealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident: retention expectations for session snapshots

Ben —

Thanks again for the quick response last night. Our security team is doing a post-incident evidence collection and we need guidance on a couple items so we can align with our legal/regulatory obligations:

1) What exact artifacts are you preserving by default after an incident (e.g., full session traces, ephemeral session snapshots, KV cache metadata)?
2) For ephemeral session snapshots (sub-second snapshots used for replay), what is Redwood's recommended hold window for forensic analysis before deletion?
3) If we request a longer hold window for specific accounts, what is the SLA and process (docs, chain-of-custody, cost implication)?

Can you point me to the manifest of items preserved and the timeline we should expect? We may request a short extension on a subset for our regulator.

—Tim
Tim Browne
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Acme Health
security@acmehealth.com

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-incident: retention expectations for session snapshots

Tim / Ben —

Thanks — adding detail from the IR playbook. High-level summary:

- What we preserve by default: request logs (request metadata, timestamps, prompt hashes), model response trunks (token sequences), session snapshots (ephemeral state used for in-flight replay), and KV-cache metadata. We do NOT by default retain full user PII payloads beyond what was written to the request logs (we redact according to configured PII filters at ingestion).

- Default hold window: for customers on hosted plans, ephemeral session snapshots and related in-memory artifacts are placed on a short forensic hold for 7 days post-incident by default to allow triage and replay. Request logs and token sequences are retained according to the customer's configured retention (typical default: 90 days) unless otherwise contracted.

- Scoped extension process: for an account-specific extension, we require a signed request (DocuSign link), justification, and approval from the security/compliance team. Typical extension SLA: 48 hours to acknowledge; 5 business days to provision a scoped extended hold and provide chain-of-custody export. There is a small engineering-assisted cost for keeping large KV snapshots beyond 30 days — we can provide a cost estimate once you confirm size/scope.

Attachments provided: a small sample of the snapshot manifest (subset_logs_sample.txt) and the chain_of_custody_template.pdf for your legal team.

Notes/risks: if you need cross-border transfer for custody (e.g., move snapshots to Acme's AWS bucket in eu-central-1), talk to Ops first — there are residency checks.

Soojin Lee
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

[Attachment: subset_logs_sample.txt (text/plain)]
[Attachment: chain_of_custody_template.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, Tim Browne <tim.browne@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:10:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident: retention expectations for session snapshots

Tim / team —

Two quick clarifications from the compliance side for healthcare/regulatory customers:

1) If Acme requests preservation beyond the default 7-day snapshot hold, we will:
   - Create an account-level evidence hold record in our IR system with explicit start/end dates, scope (customer id + snapshot IDs), and assign an engineer for export.
   - Retain exported artifacts in a locked S3 bucket with versioning disabled and restricted IAM until transfer or deletion.

2) Requests longer than 30 days may trigger an elevated review (privacy and legal); we will notify Acme and propose either an encrypted escrow to your KMS or timed deletion with attestation.

Please confirm if Acme needs us to initiate the 48-hour extension workflow; if so, Ben please create a signed request or forward the Go/No-Go from their legal team.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the patience. Short answer for your regulator: default snapshot hold = 7 days; request-initiated extension available with 48-hour ack and up to 30 days with light engineering support. Beyond 30 days we escalate to legal and can offer encrypted escrow options.

Next actions I propose:
- If Acme wants the extension, reply to this thread with a signed request or approval from legal and we will start the 48-hour workflow.
- I attached the manifest we discussed, a small sample of the preserved snapshot text, and our standard chain-of-custody PDF for your records.

I'll keep this thread in my mailbox and will escalate to Ops if we get the signed extension.
